column4: Esus gifted the Svartalfar, the winter court side of the elven civil war, with a breed of large panthers that were strong mounts as well as powerful attackers in their own right. A Nyxkin is a Svartalfar warrior who is bound to one of these panthers. The bond is so great that if either side dies, the other will as well. -- The Bestiary of Erebus
A Minotaur is a tall humanoid with the head of a bull. They are vigilante guardians, and outside of being unable to resist a fight they mind they are reliable soldiers. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Esus traveled to the dark hell of Agares only to find it deserted and in ruin. Disliking such a barren world Esus breathed life into the dust and a people half-formed appeared, shadows of a lost people. These people he named the Mistforms and he brought them into Erebus. Mistforms can attack people, but if left alone typically avoid any contact with men and go through their own patterns and habits with little regard for the surrounding world. These habits seem to have little purpose and many suspect they are dreaming they are in a world that no longer exists. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

The Stygian Guard are the silent servants of Hastur. They exhibit no attempts at communication and little evidence of thought outside of their ability to ruthlessly follow commands. When they aren't being commanded they seek out pools or other bodies of water and sink unmoving to the bottom unless disturbed. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

A mix of eagles and lions, griffons make loyal mounts and pets to those who are able to tame them. They enjoy dangerous flying so less reckless riders will probably only ride a griffon once. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Sea Serpents can grow to be large enough to swallow entire ships whole and they release thousands of eggs during their mating cycles. It is only their frequent clashes with each other and the lack of food in their environment that keeps their numbers under control. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Use Pyre Zombies as expendable front line troops. They are stronger than Men-At Arms, if you include their fire damage, and when defeated will explode, damaging all units (enemy and friendly) within a tile of the zombie. They require both Fire and Death mana to train, and are not available to players of the Good alignment. They are Undead units, and so are vulnerable to the Undead Slaying promotion and the Destroy Undead Spell. The Overcouncil's resolution against Death mana blocks its members from training these units.

Magnadine's horsemanship is legendary, but he is more renowned for leading mercenaries to wealth and glory. Sellswords often rip up contracts to join his company. His charisma inspires loyalty that is worth far more than gold.

Baron Duin Halfmorn was a fearsome warlord during the Age of Magic. He hosted lavish banquets after his victories, where he and his generals feasted on the bodies of the vanquished. In time his generals' ambition grew to match his own. They turned on him in a bloody civil war. Duin won the war but lost his empire; he sat alone in the end, feasting on his generals' corpses. [PARAGRAPH:1]Ancient legends tell of Duin's cruelty, cannibalism, and worship of Camulos, but they do not relate his darkest secret. The God of Strife rewarded the Baron's devotion with the curse of Lycanthropy, yet let him control his bestial nature well enough to keep it hidden from the world. Duin was not the first werewolf, nor last, but was the greatest. [PARAGRAPH:1]The horrific Duin did die, as all mortals do, but would not be allowed to rest in peace. His soul fought for centuries in Hell, before returning to the world of the living. In a time of dire need, desperate mages performed rites to bring back the greatest, most feared general of history. [PARAGRAPH:1]Mortal magic may resurrect only the dead whose spirits linger in Erebus. Without divine intervention, it can never draw a soul back from beyond the plane. Camulos sent the Baron back on a mission to revive lycanthropy. Werewolves went extinct during the Age of Ice. Every infection in the current epidemic can be clearly traced back to Halfmorn himself. His true nature is now known, and rightly feared.

Duin is now a melee unit instead of a beast, so he cannot so easily be captured by Beastmasters, but he is still a werewolf. Living units that he slays, or even those that slay him, risk becoming infected with Lycanthropy. He is the Alpha Werewolf, who can dominate other lycanthropes to make them join his pack. Ravenous Werewolves are usually born rebellious, but they would not dare rebel against the Baron Halfmorn.

[TAB]The Frost Speakers, disciples of Mulcarn, were tolerated by most nations in the Age of Magic. They would pledge allegiance to no sovereign, but they did not speak sedition, either. Well beyond stoic in their demeanor, followers of Winter lost passion of all sorts. Initiation to this order involved bathing in icy waters overnight. Those who survived the 'baptism' usually had their outlook changed dramatically by it, without need of theological debate. [PARAGRAPH:1]These cold men now lead the armies of their god. Slow to adapt to their enemies' tactics, their strength lies in unflinching rationality, carrying out their plans unhindered by fear, ambition, or personal attachment. They will patch up wounded soldiers with divine aid of their god-king, but evidence suggests their compassion is something to be desired. More than once Amurite recon patrols have found badly wounded Illian warriors buried in the snow--occasionally still breathing.

[TAB]The protection of our national wealth demands that we restrict our trading, so as to prevent other nations from profiting from the work our faithful citizens have done. Any foreign power is a potential adversary, a vicious predator probing for weaknesses and biding its time. To hand it weapons and tools is to invite disaster. [PARAGRAPH:1]-Arian Kothrax, High Councilor, Steward of Inequity[PARAGRAPH:2]Trade has ever been the extinguisher of war, the eradicator of prejudice, the diffuser of knowledge. [PARAGRAPH:1]Is it not evident that the impoverishment and dependence of labor are abnormal conditions resulting from restrictions and usurpations, and that instead of accepting protection, what labor should demand is freedom. That those who advocate any extension of freedom choose to go no further than suits their own special purpose is no reason why freedom itself should be distrusted. [PARAGRAPH:1]-Henry George

A fire ship or fireship, used in the days of wooden rowed or sailing ships, was a ship filled with combustibles, deliberately set on fire and steered (or, where possible, allowed to drift) into an enemy fleet, in order to destroy ships, or to create panic and make the enemy break formation. Ships used as fire ships were usually old and worn out or purpose-built inexpensive vessels. An explosion ship or hellburner was a variation on the fire ship, intended to cause damage by blowing up in proximity to enemy ships.

Fire Ships are cheap expendable alternatives to more conventional naval combat, and a good way to get rid of otherwise obsolete vessels. When defeated they will explode, damaging all units (enemy and friendly) nearby. They can be produded through either arcane or mundane means, using either Fire Mana or Gunpowder.

Sarabride outlaws magic entirely and has an army of witch hunters specifically trained to kill mages. She also has a formidable force of cannons and steampunk style riflemen and pistoleers. Unknown to most, a small group of true angels of Bhall serve, guard and protect her.

No mortals are better trained than Witch Hunters for the task of protecting society from rogue sorcerers. Unfortunately, they tend to be cruel and corrupt. Even honest ones are often overzealous, failing to distinguish between good and evil uses of magic and more willing to condemn a hundred innocents than let one guilty party go free. Employing them especially angers those leaders whose political power depends upon arcane might.
Enlist the Nightwatch: A Nightwatch unit is provided to every member who pays, and the state religion requirement for training them is waived.
Enlist the Radiant Guard: A Radiant Guard unit is provided to every member, and the state religion requirement for training them is waived.
